claims: Transfuse red blood cells for severe anemia (hemoglobin 7.1 g/dL, hematocrit 20.9%) in the setting of active bleeding risk and coagulopathy.
Initiate broad-spectrum antibiotics (e.g., meropenem) for suspected sepsis given fever, leukocytosis, lactic acidosis, and hypotension.
Administer intravenous fluids and vasopressors (norepinephrine) to maintain mean arterial pressure >65 mmHg given hypotension (MAP 44-53 mmHg) and lactic acidosis.
Reverse coagulopathy with vitamin K and fresh frozen plasma or prothrombin complex concentrate given INR 4.1 and elevated PT/PTT.
Obtain blood cultures and repeat lactate to guide sepsis management.
Adjust ventilator settings to maintain adequate oxygenation and lung-protective ventilation given plateau pressure 29 cmH2O and PEEP 8-10 cmH2O.
Monitor serum potassium and renal function closely given hyperkalemia (5.2 mEq/L) and acute kidney injury (creatinine 3.6 mg/dL).
Monitor blood glucose and administer insulin as needed for hyperglycemia (glucose 284 mg/dL).
Provide stress ulcer prophylaxis with a proton pump inhibitor (e.g., pantoprazole) given mechanical ventilation and coagulopathy.
Perform daily sedation interruption and assess readiness for extubation given goal RASS -2 and current RASS -5.
